review.mathCheck: The factorization (b−1)(a−c)=13 exhausts b=0,2,14,−12. The last gives (a,b,c)=(−9,−12,−8), satisfying all equations and yielding 276, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 17, page 10: exploit the prime difference and check four signed-divisor cases. The candidate expands the excluded factor pairs and uniquely derives the surviving solution.
review.annotationCheck: The case analysis is exhaustive over integers, including negative values. Primality and common-factor extraction genuinely support the assessed integer-equation method; the final substitution verifies feasibility.
